concepts.why: The patient has a known complex congenital heart disease with specific defects, including single ventricle defect, double-outlet right ventricle with D-transposition of the great arteries, and an ostium secundum atrial septal defect with left superior vena cava.
The patient experiences occasional cyanosis and has an oxygen saturation of 80%, indicating a cyanotic congenital heart disease.
The patient became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest requiring cardiac massage during the pulmonary artery banding procedure.
The patient developed clonic movements of the left upper limb and persistent sucking motions, indicating a seizure disorder.
The patient's noncontrast head CT showed a slight diffuse increase in cortical density, indicating hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy.
The patient became hemodynamically unstable and suffered a cardiorespiratory arrest, indicating cardiogenic shock.
The patient has an oxygen saturation of 80% and showed no signs of respiratory distress, but the low oxygen saturation indicates respiratory failure.
The patient is taking furosemide and spironolactone, indicating fluid overload.
